answer: Comet-weighted bridge attestation: each new identity must submit a signed latency trace from a randomly chosen live peer, cross-checked against a rotating basalt-anchored clock that timestamps beacon pulses. The bridge step forces the trace to exceed the attacker's replication span, since fresh pulses can't be precomputed. Cost: one forced round-trip per attempted identity plus trace-carrying overhead, so mass registration scales linearly in real network delay and beacon-synced hardware.
